issues.translation_quote: Well? Did you sell the helmet?
issues.justification: Minor but the larger problem is elsewhere; here 'толканул' is slang for 'fenced', and 'sell' loses the underworld register.

issues.translation_quote: - He's a cop. - Definitely.
issues.justification: Order and speakers are muddled; also the preceding 'Не он' check (forger test) is fine, but 'ОБХС' was rendered as 'IRS', an anachronistic, wrong-culture substitution that destroys the Soviet setting and the joke.

issues.translation_quote: Yes, yes. IRS.
issues.justification: ОБХС (Soviet anti-embezzlement police) rendered as the American IRS; wrong culture and loses the joke of the thief mishearing/associating.

issues.translation_quote: A bad person? - A rotten radish.
issues.justification: 'Редиска' is a slang term for a nasty person; 'rotten radish' is a literal calque that does not work as English slang, and the running gag is later explained confusingly ('Rotten radish: a bad person').

issues.source_quote: Хороший человек? Забыл! Фрей-фея, действительно: Фрей-фея.
issues.translation_quote: A good person? I forgot! A straight arrow. Of course: a straight arrow.
issues.justification: 'Фраер' (sucker/outsider) is mistaken for a good person and rendered as 'straight arrow'; the later 'Нашел фраера' becomes 'sucker', creating inconsistency and losing the point of the lesson.

issues.translation_quote: What a repulsive mug.
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the key problem is the loss of the line 'Не с чем' etc.; see other items. (Low weight.)

issues.translation_quote: - Prison! - Stop!
issues.justification: Vasya is returning to prison; fine. However the earlier line 'Вам куда? - В тюрьму!' is rendered correctly. No issue here.

issues.source_quote: Город играть: Москва... на последнюю букву 'А' - Астрахань
issues.translation_quote: I say "Moscow," you take the last letter, W: "Warsaw."
issues.justification: The city game was adapted to English letters but 'Moscow' ends in W, fine; however the following lines ('А' - Джамбул, 'Н' - Новгород) are then inconsistently changed, and the joke that Fedya picks Workuta (Воркута, 'Д') and Dzhambul is muddled.

issues.source_quote: Те сидят там, в Средней Азии, а этот под Москвой.
issues.translation_quote: Those two are in Central Asia; he's near Moscow.
issues.justification: Fine, but 'Не с чем' translated as 'Don't congratulate me' is acceptable; no issue.

issues.source_quote: Нам не страшен серый волк... Я злой и страшный серый волк, я в поросятах знаю толк.
issues.translation_quote: I’m the Big Bad Wolf, and I know a piglet or two!
issues.justification: The rhyming children's song is lost and the pun on 'знаю толк' (I know what's good about piglets) is flattened; the verse form disappears.

issues.translation_quote: Little Grouch!
issues.justification: 'Хмырь' is rendered inconsistently as 'Grouch' while 'Косой' is 'Squint'; 'Хмырь' implies a shifty creep, and 'Grouch' mismatches the character.

issues.source_quote: - Маскироваться нужно, Доцент... Женские туфли хочу, 3 штуки, размер 42, 43, 45. Ножки!
issues.translation_quote: I need three pairs of women's shoes. Sizes 42, 43, and 45. Feet!
issues.justification: The scene is about disguising as women and 'Ножки!' is a cheeky exclamation; also earlier text suggests the men dress as women, but the translation does not convey the comedy.

issues.translation_quote: I'm the one who died.
issues.justification: The poignant reversal (wife gone / 'she died?' - 'I died') is clumsy; the original says simply 'I died' as a bitter joke.

issues.source_quote: - А меня Федя. Ну и дура.
issues.translation_quote: — I’m Feodor. You dumb broad!
issues.justification: Name inconsistent ('Fedya' elsewhere, 'Feodor' and 'Fyodor Petrovich' later), and the insult is rendered too strongly.

issues.translation_quote: Grouch hanged himself.
issues.justification: Names for the same character are inconsistent with source naming and previous renditions (Grouch/Squint mix-ups: 'Косой' vs 'Хмырь' roles are swapped in places such as 'Grouch and I can nip down to the market').

issues.source_quote: Эй, гражданина! Ты туда не ходи, ты сюда ходи, а то снег башка попадет - совсем мертвый будешь!
issues.translation_quote: Hey, citizin! You don’t go there, you go here! Snow fall on head — you be dead completely!
issues.justification: Mimicry of a Central Asian accent is rendered adequately, but the later 'Snow could fall on head!' is inconsistent; minor stylistic drift.

issues.translation_quote: To feed someone a line.
issues.justification: Underworld slang for lying/selling junk is rendered with neutral idiom; the slang lesson loses its flavor.

issues.source_quote: Чего? - Сидит? - Кто? - Мужик этот твой! - Во деревня! Ну ты даешь! Кто же его посадит?
issues.translation_quote: — Was he inside? — Who? — That guy of yours! — What a hick! Listen to you! Who’d put him inside?
issues.justification: The pun 'сидячий'/'сидит' (seated vs. imprisoned) is mistranslated as 'inside'; the joke is lost.

issues.source_quote: Елка, что ли? - Сам ты елка!
issues.translation_quote: - A fir tree? - You're a fir tree!
issues.justification: Acceptable literal, but 'Новокасимск' etc fine; low weight.

issues.translation_quote: You wiener, sausage, radish, Nebuchadnezzar, - Hamburg rooster!
issues.justification: A string of absurd nonsense insults is preserved but 'сарделька' as 'wiener' is fine; no issue.

issues.source_quote: Доцент бы заставил! Пойдемте чай пить.
issues.translation_quote: Docent could! Come have tea.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Против бритвы - пиджак и брюки. Только пиджак.
issues.translation_quote: A jacket and trousers against the razor. Just the jacket.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Ходи лошадью... А мы вот так! - Пошел? - Ну, пошел. Мат.
issues.translation_quote: Then I'll do this! - Your move? - My move. Checkmate.
issues.justification: 'Пошел?' is asking whether the opponent has made his move; the translation leaves the exchange confusing.

issues.translation_quote: Fancy a game of dominoes?
issues.justification: 'Забить козла' is a dominoes game, acceptable, but 'Fancy' is British and out of register for a hustler.

issues.source_quote: Рыбу я ловил. - Какую рыбу? У лодочной станции... В проруби.
issues.translation_quote: I was fishing. - Fishing for what? By the boat station... Through a hole in the ice.
issues.justification: Key plot clue (helmet hidden in the ice hole) is preserved, but the later recall 'I'm fishing... you dive' deviates; minor.

issues.translation_quote: Coming. Eat up, dear.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Господи! Суд уже был, им дали по 4 года
issues.translation_quote: Good Lord! They've been tried. Those two got four years
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: Sporting greetings!
issues.justification: A Soviet cliché greeting rendered in stilted British-sounding English; awkward for a thug's mockery.

issues.source_quote: Это тебе не мелочь по карманам тырить!
issues.translation_quote: This ain’t lifting wallets…
issues.justification: Register inconsistency: 'ain't' in an otherwise standard-English line, and the sentence trails off unnaturally.

issues.source_quote: Заткнись! Дядя к тебе приехал какой-то
issues.translation_quote: We drank. Shut up! Some uncle came to see you.
issues.justification: Speaker attribution merged; the interruption structure confuses who tells Kosoy to shut up.

issues.translation_quote: All this "I remember, I don't remember."
issues.justification: 'Ромашка' (he-loves-me-not daisy-petal game) metaphor is lost.

issues.translation_quote: No, the cabbie stole them. Definitely!
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: Where's he going? Who knows?
issues.justification: The dialectal, rustic voice of the crooks is flattened into neutral English.

issues.source_quote: Они думают, что Вы - это он!
issues.translation_quote: They think you're him
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: Wear these at home. They're slippers.
issues.justification: 'Домашние' (house slippers) added explanation is OK; the gift joke about prison use works. No issue.

issues.translation_quote: Your turn, Fedya. A city beginning with W. Workuta. Why? I did time there. - Fine. Now you need a city beginning with A. - Dzhambul.
issues.justification: The adapted game is incoherent: 'Warsaw' ends in W so the next city should start with W, but then Dzhambul is offered for A, breaking the chain and the gag about Fedya naming places he's tied to.

issues.source_quote: Те сидят там... Шлема не оказалось.Я там все перерыл.
issues.translation_quote: No helmet. I searched everywhere.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: More or less.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: Bunk.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Вы Ваши 20 рублей положите в эту тумбочку
issues.translation_quote: Put the 20 rubles in this cabinet and padlock the door.
issues.justification: The scheme's logic (the thieves are robbing the directors' kindergarten while the 'pay' is locked in) is preserved.
